Subject: Post-call: model fit + next steps (RetailCo)

Alex / Jordan 1 thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary
- Use case: customer support summarization + suggested replies across RetailCo's returns flow
- Current integration: Redwood hosted endpoint with model-family `retail-synth` (we were on v2.0 until last week)
- Primary success metrics: summary ROUGE/ROUGE-L, reply correctness rate on 1k prompt eval set, and median latency < 120ms

Action items I take away
1) Send you the eval prompt set and latest benchmark diffs (attached).
2) Recommend trying `retail-synth-v2` (quantized) + prompt set v3 vs `retail-synth-v1` for a quick A/B.
3) If you see anything that looks like a quality regression after our rollout, please flag immediately 1 we can pin a previous model version or roll back while we investigate.

Attachments: retailco_prompt_set_v3.txt, benchmark_diffs_20260730.csv

Next steps
- I'll loop in Dev to share the benchmark diffs and a rollback plan we can use if needed (target: canary rollback within 2 hours).
- Alex/Jordan: Can you run the v2 inference on a small batch from your prod data and share a few examples by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks 1 chat soon.

1
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@retailco.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit + next steps (RetailCo)

Thanks for the recap, Marissa. We ran a small batch overnight against v2 and noticed a noticeable drop in reply correctness for our returns domain 1 wrong suggested policies in ~8% of cases (previously ~2%). We attached two examples inline below.

Example 1: customer says they returned an item but tracking shows delivered -> model suggested 'refund immediately' instead of 'confirm receipt'
Example 2: model omitted asking for order number when customer asked about exchange window

This lines up with our internal QA where we saw more hallucinations and trimmed responses since the update on Jul 30. We're pausing the wider rollout until we get clarity 1 can you confirm if any model architecture or prompt template changes were pushed around Jul 30?

Appreciate a quick look.

Alex
Head of CX Automation, RetailCo
alex.kim@retailco.com

Folks 1 forwarding RetailCo's note. They see a regression after our Jul 30 push. Can we triage quickly? I pulled the diffs from the inference pipeline and attached the benchmark CSV and a draft rollback plan.

What I need from eng (priority order):
- Quick assessment (are there model-side changes or prompt template changes on Jul 30?).
- If model update: recommend rollback vs pinning and estimated time to rollback for a canary vs full rollback.
- If prompt/template change: provide a short patch plan.

Attachments: benchmark_diffs_20260730.csv, rollback_plan_v1.docx

Timeline: RetailCo wants action ASAP 1 ideally canary rollback within 2 hours.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call: model fit + next steps (RetailCo)

Checked the deployment logs and model registry: we rolled `retail-synth` from v2.0 -> v2.1 on 2026-07-30 at 02:14 UTC. v2.1 includes a tokenizer update and a light prompting-layer change to trim system prompts for latency improvements. 

Preliminary findings: 
- Benchmark diffs show a drop in token-level precision on return-specific prompts (see attached CSV) 1 aligns with Alex's examples.
- The tokenizer update changed a few token boundaries for terms like 'return' vs 'returned' which can affect few-shot prompt matching.

Options and ETA: 
1) Canary rollback to v2.0 for RetailCo route only (recommended immediate mitigation) 1 ETA: ~45 minutes to flip traffic to pinned v2.0 for 5% canary.
2) Full rollback to v2.0 globally 1 ETA: 2-3 hours (requires coordinated cache warm restart).
3) Patch prompting layer to restore the previous system prompt length/format and re-test 1 ETA: 1-2 hours to dev + 30-60 mins for canary test.

I recommend option 1 now (canary rollback to v2.0) + option 3 in parallel to harden prompt behavior. I attached a quick rollback playbook (rollback_plan_v1.docx).

I'll open JIRA-INF-892 to track the work and update RetailCo after the canary is live.

1 Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Alex / Jordan 1 quick update and next steps: 

Status: Dev confirmed the Jul 30 change for `retail-synth-v2.1` included a tokenizer and prompt trim that likely caused the regression. We've kicked off a 5% canary rollback to v2.0 for your route now (ETA ~45 mins).

What to expect
- We'll monitor the same prompt set v3 against the canary and share diffs in the next 90 minutes.
- If the canary shows improvements, we'll expand to full rollback within the day.
- Parallel: Dev is implementing a prompt-layer patch (option 3) to avoid future trims; ETA 1-2 hours.

Next steps for RetailCo
- Please send any additional example failures to this thread (or upload to the Drive folder).
- We'll share a post-mortem with diffs and a recommended pinning policy (we can pin v2.0 for your route until the patch is validated).

Appreciate the quick flagging, Alex 1 we'll be in touch shortly with the canary results.

1
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
